These are distinct protocols. Select one to inspect its Stage 1 target and Stage 2 input; existing results retain their recorded protocol.

STAGE 1

Write the whole-module specification

InputClean module RTL: stage1/design.v
InstructionWrite a self-contained specification of the WHOLE design in design.v: its interface, parameters, and observable behavior, including clock/reset behavior when present. Return prose, not RTL implementation code. A separate isolated call will receive only your whole-design specification and a masked version of this design.

Stored wording: stage1/TASK.md

OutputGenerated whole-module specification (prose).
Read input: stage1/design.v · Open raw
module mg_01680 (input [2:0] state,input prefix,input need_modrm,input need_off,input need_imm,input end_seq,input [5:0] ftype,input of,input next_in_opco,input next_in_exec,input block,input div_exc,input intr,input ifl,output [2:0] next_state);
parameter opcod_st = 3'h0; 
  parameter modrm_st = 3'h1; 
  parameter offse_st = 3'h2; 
  parameter immed_st = 3'h3; 
  parameter execu_st = 3'h4; 
  wire into, end_instr, end_into; 
  wire [2:0] n_state; 
  wire intr_ifl; 
  assign into = (ftype==6'b111_010); 
  assign end_into = into ? ~of : end_seq; 
  assign end_instr = !div_exc && !intr_ifl && end_into && !next_in_exec; 
  assign intr_ifl = intr & ifl; 
 assign n_state = (state == opcod_st) ? (prefix ? opcod_st: (next_in_opco ? opcod_st: (need_modrm ? modrm_st: (need_off ? offse_st: (need_imm ? immed_st : execu_st))))) 
 : (state == modrm_st) ? (need_off ? offse_st: (need_imm ? immed_st : execu_st)) 
  : (state == offse_st) ? (need_imm ? immed_st : execu_st) 
  : (state == immed_st) ? (execu_st) 
  : (end_instr ? opcod_st : execu_st); 
  assign next_state = block ? state : n_state; 
 endmodule
STAGE 2

Complete the module

InputThe generated Stage 1 text plus masked module rtl: stage2_template/design.v. Required top module: mg_01680.
InstructionRestore the masked functional logic in design.v using the supplied whole-design specification and retained RTL context. Return the complete corrected RTL with the same top module and interface. The default configuration is scored using the original design verification setup.

Stored wording: stage2_template/TASK.md

OutputComplete RTL module with the masked logic restored.

parameter opcod_st = 3'h0; 
  parameter modrm_st = 3'h1; 
  parameter offse_st = 3'h2; 
  parameter immed_st = 3'h3; 
  parameter execu_st = 3'h4; 
  wire into, end_instr, end_into; 
  wire [2:0] n_state; 
  wire intr_ifl; 
  assign into = (ftype==6'b111_010); 
  assign end_into = into ? ~of : end_seq; 
  assign end_instr = !div_exc && !intr_ifl && end_into && !next_in_exec; 
  assign intr_ifl = intr & ifl; 
 assign n_state = /* RTL_BENCHLS_MASK: restore expression */; 
  assign next_state = block ? state : n_state; 
 endmodule
Stage 1 output → abstraction gate → fresh Stage 2 input. The intermediate text is generated separately for each model/attempt. It is not a prefilled golden description. Stage 2 receives neither the clean RTL nor the Stage 1 conversation.

Private final evaluation

Reference RTLprivate/golden.v

entry_point:
Agent entry point — start here

Round-trip tasks have two separate agent entry points:

  1. Stage 1: stage1/TASK.md
  2. Stage 2: stage2_template/TASK.md

Follow the stage panels below for each stage’s input files and required output. The accepted Stage 1 text is supplied to a fresh Stage 2 context; Stage 2 does not receive clean RTL or the Stage 1 conversation.

These links are the whole-module case-package instructions. The specialist/targeted view instead uses runner-generated masked-region prompts, shown in its stage panels.

A stored instruction is distinct from the runtime launch message, which can add framing and execution limits. The agent uses the harness’s file-reading tools to inspect available inputs. The file list also includes human-review reference and oracle assets that must not be given to the evaluated agent.
